glass_sam: Previous notes suggested sink_k1 for evening queries based on Day 12 feedback. Day 13 feedback at 19:33 showed dining_table_d1, and at 22:09 showed nightstand_b1. The location is highly erratic and does not follow a consistent time-based pattern (dining vs. sink vs. nightstand). Do not default to any single spot. Check dining_table_d1, sink_k1, and nightstand_b1 as equally likely candidates for evening queries.

book_sam: Previous notes indicated movement to bed_b1 in the evening for reading. Day 13 feedback at 20:57 showed armchair_l1. This contradicts the previous assumption that the book moves to the bedroom. The book may remain in the living room for evening reading. Check armchair_l1 or couch_l1 for evening queries rather than bed_b1.

charger_sam: Previous notes indicated alternation between desk_b1 and nightstand_b1 in the late evening. Day 8 feedback at 21:53 showed nightstand_b1. No new contradictory evidence today. Continue checking nightstand_b1 for queries after 21:00, but remain open to desk_b1 if the pattern shifts.

mug_sam: Previous notes indicated movement between kitchen_table_k1 (morning) and coffee_table_l1 (evening). Day 9 feedback at 07:46 showed kitchen_table_k1. No new contradictory evidence today. Continue checking kitchen_table_k1 for morning queries and coffee_table_l1 for evening queries.

General Observation: Item locations are dynamic. Glass_sam is the most erratic, appearing at dining_table_d1, nightstand_b1, and sink_k1. Book_sam has shifted from bedroom to living room spots. Prioritize recent feedback. For evening queries, check dining_table_d1/sink_k1/nightstand_b1 for glass_sam, armchair_l1 for book_sam, nightstand_b1 for charger_sam, and coffee_table_l1 for mug_sam. Avoid assuming static locations for glass_sam and book_sam.
